en.headline: Customs seize two live cats from mainland passenger at Lo Wu
en.dek: A 44-year-old man was arrested after officers found the animals, valued at about HK$2,000, in his luggage at the control point on Sunday; the case was referred to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department.
body: Hong Kong Customs intercepted a 44-year-old mainland male passenger at the Lo Wu Control Point arrival hall on Sunday and seized two suspected illegally imported live cats from his personal luggage.

The animals had an estimated market value of about HK$2,000. The passenger was arrested on the spot and the case has been handed over to the Agriculture, Fisheries and Conservation Department for further investigation.

Customs reminded the public that importing animals into Hong Kong without a valid permit is an offence. Under the Rabies Regulation, anyone convicted of illegally importing animals, carcasses or animal products faces a maximum fine of HK$50,000 and one year’s imprisonment.

zh.headline: 海關羅湖截獲內地男旅客行李藏兩活貓
zh.dek: 44歲內地男旅客周日在羅湖管制站入境大堂被截查，行李內檢獲兩隻懷疑非法進口活貓，市值約2,000港元，男子當場被捕，案件交漁護署跟進。
body: 香港海關周日在羅湖管制站入境大堂截查一名44歲抵港內地男旅客，在其個人行李內檢獲兩隻懷疑非法進口的活貓，估計市值約2,000港元。
該名旅客隨即被捕，案件已轉交漁農自然護理署作進一步調查。
海關提醒市民，任何人未領有有效許可證而將動物輸入香港即屬違法。根據《狂犬病規例》，非法輸入動物、動物屍體或動物產品，一經定罪，最高可被判罰款5萬港元及監禁一年。
